policy_note: This manifest exists to answer one question deterministically, the same way on every developer machine: for a given exact commit SHA, what quality-gate outcomes were verified on a canonical, trusted execution environment (GitHub Actions CI)? It is consulted by scripts/quality/bys360_score_reconcile_v1.py's resolve_evidence() before falling back to the current machine's own local gate execution. This session has no direct network/API access to GitHub Actions, so every entry below with evidence_type=REMOTE_CI_VERIFIED is recorded with provenance=USER_SUPPLIED_REMOTE_PROOF -- it was manually reported by the project owner in chat, not independently fetched or verified by this tooling. That distinction is preserved in every entry and must never be silently upgraded to look machine-verified. No entry in this file was fabricated: only gate outcomes the user actually stated are present here, each tied to the exact commit_sha the user stated it for. Entries are never expired by age (schema_version 1.0 uses exact-commit-SHA matching as the only freshness criterion, per policy -- see docs/governance/BYS360_SCORING_METHODOLOGY_V1.md 'Evidence precedence' section) but ARE strictly rejected as stale the instant the scored commit's SHA no longer matches, with no branch-name or recency substitute.

non_gate_context_only.label: Type check service layer
non_gate_context_only.reason_not_mapped: SCOPE MISMATCH, deliberately not mapped to mypy_full_scope: this CI job type-checks the service layer only, while mypy_full_scope scores mypy across app + tests + scripts (the whole repo). Treating a narrower-scope PASS as equivalent evidence for the broader-scope gate would silently overstate verified coverage, so it is recorded here as context only and does not satisfy mypy_full_scope's canonical evidence requirement.
